def _directed_div_vectors(fmt):
    """Hand-verified directed vectors for division (5.4.1)."""
    w = fmt.width
    neg = lambda x: x ^ (1 << (w - 1))
    m0 = fmt.W_MANT
    m1 = _norm1(fmt)          # 1.0
    m1s = neg(m1)
    m2 = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias + 1, 0, fmt)         # 2.0
    m4 = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias + 2, 0, fmt)         # 4.0
    m05 = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias - 1, 0, fmt)        # 0.5
    m025 = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias - 2, 0, fmt)       # 0.25
    maxf = max_finite_bits(0, fmt)
    maxs = neg(maxf)
    maxm = (1 << m0) - 1
    z = encode_zero(0, fmt)
    zs = encode_zero(1, fmt)
    inf = encode_inf(0, fmt)
    infs = encode_inf(1, fmt)
    qnan = encode_nan(0, fmt)
    minn = encode_finite(0, 1, 0, fmt)                  # min normal
    maxsn = encode_finite(0, 0, maxm, fmt)              # max subnormal
    minsn = encode_finite(0, 0, 1, fmt)                 # min subnormal
    inv = 1 << formats.FLAG_INVALID
    d0 = 1 << formats.FLAG_DIV0
    ine = 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT
    uf = 1 << formats.FLAG_UNDERFLOW
    v = []

    # --- zero products/quotients: sign is the XOR of the operand signs (6.3)
    v += [
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, z, m1, z, 0, "0/1 = +0"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, zs, m1, zs, 0, "-0/1 = -0"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, z, m1s, zs, 0, "0/-1 = -0"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1, z, inf, d0, "1/0 -> +inf, div0 (7.3)"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1, zs, infs, d0, "1/-0 -> -inf, div0"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1s, z, infs, d0, "-1/0 -> -inf, div0"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1s, zs, inf, d0, "-1/-0 -> +inf, div0"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, z, z, qnan, inv, "0/0 -> qNaN, invalid (7.2f)"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, z, zs, qnan, inv, "0/-0 -> qNaN, invalid (7.2f)"),
    ]

    # --- infinities (6.3, 7.2f)
    v += [
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, inf, m2, inf, 0, "inf/2 = +inf"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, infs, m2, infs, 0, "-inf/2 = -inf"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m2, inf, z, 0, "2/inf = +0"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m2, infs, zs, 0, "2/-inf = -0"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, inf, z, inf, 0, "inf/0 = +inf (not div0)"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, z, inf, z, 0, "0/inf = +0"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, inf, inf, qnan, inv, "inf/inf -> qNaN, invalid (7.2f)"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, infs, infs, qnan, inv, "-inf/-inf -> qNaN, invalid"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, inf, infs, qnan, inv, "inf/-inf -> qNaN, invalid"),
    ]

    # --- NaNs (6.2.3, 7.2a)
    v += [
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, qnan, m1, qnan, 0, "qNaN/1 -> qNaN"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1, qnan, qnan, 0, "1/qNaN -> qNaN"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, inf, qnan, qnan, 0, "inf/qNaN -> qNaN"),
    ]
    if w == 32:
        v += [
            (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, 0x7FC00001, m2, 0x7FC00001, 0, "qNaN payload passthrough"),
            (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, 0x7F800001, m2, 0x7FC00001, inv, "sNaN -> qNaN, invalid"),
            (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m2, 0xFF80000F, 0x7FC0000F, inv, "sNaN payload kept, invalid"),
        ]

    # --- exact quotients (RNE)
    v += [
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1, m1, m1, 0, "1/1 = 1"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m2, m1, m2, 0, "2/1 = 2"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1, m2, m05, 0, "1/2 = 0.5"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m4, m2, m2, 0, "4/2 = 2"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m05, m2, m025, 0, "0.5/2 = 0.25"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1, m05, m2, 0, "1/0.5 = 2"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1s, m1s, m1, 0, "-1/-1 = 1"),
        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1s, m1, m1s, 0, "-1/1 = -1"),

+        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1, qnan, qnan, 0, "1/qNaN -> qNaN"),

+            (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, 0x7F800001, m2, 0x7FC00001, inv, "sNaN -> qNaN, invalid"),

+        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1, m1, m1, 0, "1/1 = 1"),
+        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m2, m1, m2, 0, "2/1 = 2"),
+        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1, m2, m05, 0, "1/2 = 0.5"),
+        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m4, m2, m2, 0, "4/2 = 2"),
+        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m05, m2, m025, 0, "0.5/2 = 0.25"),
+        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1, m05, m2, 0, "1/0.5 = 2"),

+            (OP_DIV, MODE_RP,  minsn, m2, minsn, uf | ine, "min sub/2 (RP -> min sub, underflow)"),

+        (OP_DIV, MODE_RP,  maxf, m05, inf, 0x05, "max/0.5 -> +inf (RP)"),
+        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, maxs, m05, infs, 0x05, "-max/0.5 -> -inf (RNE)"),

+        (OP_DIV, MODE_RM,  maxs, m05, infs, 0x05, "-max/0.5 (RM, negative) -> -inf"),
+        (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, maxf, m025, inf, 0x05, "max/0.25 -> +inf (RNE)"),
+    ]

+            (OP_DIV, MODE_RZ,  pe, pn100, maxf, 0x05, "e8m0: 2^EMAX/2^-100 -> max (RZ, OF+INE)"),
+            (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, pn100, pe, z, ine, "e8m0: tiny quotient -> 0 (RNE, inexact)"),
+            (OP_DIV, MODE_RP,  pn100, pe, minn, ine, "e8m0: tiny quotient -> 2^emin (RP, inexact)"),
+            (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, tie_a, tie_b, z, ine, "e8m0: half-2^emin tie -> 0 (RNE, inexact)"),
+            (OP_DIV, MODE_RNA, tie_a, tie_b, minn, ine, "e8m0: half-2^emin tie -> 2^emin (RNA)"),
+            (OP_DIV, MODE_RP,  tie_a, tie_b, minn, ine, "e8m0: half-2^emin tie -> 2^emin (RP)"),
+            (OP_DIV, MODE_RM,  tie_a, tie_b, z, ine, "e8m0: half-2^emin tie (pos) -> 0 (RM)"),

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Exhaustive all-vectors verification of the FPU add/sub/mul/div against the
bit-exact reference oracle (tests/reference/ops.py).

For each 8-bit format (1 + W_EXP + W_MANT == 8), every (op, rm, a, b)
combination -- op in {add, sub, mul, div}, all five rounding modes, and all
2^8 values for each operand -- is checked. This is 4*5*256*256 = 1,310,720
vectors per format. The cocotb VPI path is far too slow for that volume
(~0.5-2.7 s/transaction), so the DUT is exercised through a standalone
Verilator C++ harness (tests/exhaustive_main.cpp) instead.

The "1/3" generic vector is wrong. a = 0x3c00 = 1.0 (b16), b = 0x4200 = 3.0 (b16: exp field 17, mant 0x200 = 0.5 → 1.5·2^1 = 3.0). got y=0x3555, want y=0x3600.

My expected encoding for "1/3 rounds to 0.333..." was `encode_finite(0, fmt.bias - 2, 1 << (m0 - 1), fmt)` = for b16 (bias 15): encode_finite(0, 13, 512) = (1024|512)·2^(13-25) = 1536·2^-12 = 0.375. That's 0.375, not 1/3 = 0.3333! My mistake — the expected value is wrong.

The correct 1/3 in b16: 1/3 = 0.3333. Let me compute: 0.3333 = 1.3333·2^-2. significand 1.3333, mantissa = round(0.3333·2^10) = round(341.33) = 341 = 0x155. exp field = -2+15 = 13. y = (13<<10)|341 = 0x34AA... 341 = 0x155. 0x3400 | 0x155 = 0x3555. ✓ got = 0x3555. So the RTL gives 0x3555 for 1/3 in b16 — which is CORRECT (341 = 0x155 mantissa, exp 13).

So my generic vector expected value was wrong. 1/3 doesn't have a simple `encode_finite(0, bias-2, 1<<(m0-1))` form. Let me compute the generic expected value properly, or just make the vector reference-computed... The directed test is hand-verified, so let me compute the exact mantissa for 1/3 generically.

1/3 = 0.3333... In binary: 0.01010101... = 1.01010101...·2^-2. The 24-bit... wait for generic format with W_MANT = m0, p = m0+1 bits. 1/3 = 1.010101...·2^-2. The significand 1.01010101... rounds to p bits: mantissa = round(0.010101...·2^m0 · 2^... hmm.

The infinite binary expansion of 1/3 is 0.01010101... The significand is 1.010101... (bits repeating 01). Rounding to m0 fraction bits: the fraction 0.010101...01 (first m0 bits) then the pattern continues. Whether it rounds up depends on m0 parity. For b16 (m0=10): fraction bits = 0101010101, next bit = 0, then 1... So the truncated value = 0.33325195, next bit 0 → round down → mantissa 341. For b32 (m0=23): 1/3·2^23 = 2796202.67 → mantissa 2796203 (round up).

So the generic 1/3 vector depends on m0 — not a clean hand-computable closed form. Let me just remove the generic 1/3 vector (the b32-specific one covers rounding direction) and keep the exact ones. Actually, the generic "1/3 rounds" vector was meant to test a generic inexact division. Let me replace it with a simpler generic inexact case that's hand-verifiable:

Generic inexact: 1/(1 + 2^-m0) = 1 - 2^-m0 + 2^-2m0 - ... ≈ 1 - 2^-m0. Rounds to 1 - 2^-m0 (mantissa = 2^m0 - 1)... hmm, is it exact? 1/(1+2^-m0): the value ≈ 1 - 2^-m0 + 2^-2m0. Rounds to nearest representable below 1: 1 - 2^-m0 (mantissa all ones) with the 2^-2m0 term being sticky. So result = 1 - 2^-m0 = encode_finite(0, bias, (1<<m0)-1), flags = inexact. RNE (positive, value < 1, the next candidate above is 1.0): value = 1 - 2^-m0 + 2^-2m0, distance to 1-2^-m0 is 2^-2m0, distance to 1 is 2^-m0 - 2^-2m0. Closer to 1-2^-m0 → RNE rounds down → 1-2^-m0, inexact ✓. RP → round up → 1.0, inexact. RM → down → 1-2^-m0. RZ → down → 1-2^-m0.

So: b = 1 + 2^-m0 = encode_finite(0, bias, 1, fmt). a = 1.0.
- RNE: 1/(1+2^-m0) → 1 - 2^-m0, INEXACT.
- RP: → 1.0, INEXACT.
- RZ/RM: → 1 - 2^-m0, INEXACT.

Let me verify with b16: 1/(1+2^-10) = 1/1.0009765625 = 0.9990234375. 1 - 2^-10 = 0.9990234375 (mantissa 1023, exp 15). Exact? 1/(1+2^-10): (1+2^-10)^-1 = 1 - 2^-10 + 2^-20 - ... = 0.9990234375 + 0.000000953... The value = 0.99902439... vs 1-2^-10 = 0.9990234375. Value - (1-2^-10) = 2^-20·... ≈ 9.5e-7. So rounds to 1-2^-10, inexact ✓ (the RTL: norm_sticky from remainder).

This is a clean hand-verifiable vector. Let me replace the generic "1/3 rounds" with this.

Actually wait — let me double-check the RNE rounding: value = 1 - 2^-10 + 2^-20. Candidates: 1-2^-10 (mantissa 1023) and 1 (mantissa 0). Distance to 1-2^-10: 2^-20. Distance to 1: 2^-10 - 2^-20. So nearest = 1-2^-10 ✓ RNE down, INEXACT.

got = 0x3bfe: exp field 14 (0x3bfe >> 10 = 0xE = 14), mantissa 0x3fe = 1022. value = (1024+1022)·2^(14-25) = 2046·2^-11 = 0.9990234375 = 1 - 2^-10!

So BOTH are 1 - 2^-10 = 0.9990234375! The RTL produced the value in a different encoding: 0x3bfe = 1 - 2^-10 with exp field 14, mantissa 1022 (that's 1.9990234375·2^-1 = 0.9995...). Wait: (2046)·2^-11 = 2046/2048 = 0.9990234375 ✓. And 0x3fff = (2047)·2^(15-25) = 2047·2^-10 = 0.9995117. 

Hmm! 0x3fff = 2047·2^-10 = 1.999.../2... let me recompute: 2047·2^-10 = 2047/1024 = 1.9990234375? NO: 2047/1024 = 1.9990. That's NOT 1 - 2^-10! 1 - 2^-10 = 0.9990. 2047/1024 = 1.9990. These differ by factor ~2!

I made an encoding error AGAIN. `encode_finite(0, fmt.bias, (1 << m0) - 1, fmt)` = encode_finite(0, 15, 1023) = (1024|1023)·2^(15-25) = 2047·2^-10 = 1.999. That's `2 - 2^-W_MANT`, NOT `1 - 2^-W_MANT`! 

1 - 2^-m0 as a value: it's < 1, so it's NOT a normal number with exp bias! A value slightly below 1 has exp field bias-1 (leading bit 2^-1). 1 - 2^-m0 = 1.999...·2^-1 = (2 - 2^-m0)·2^-1... no wait: 1 - 2^-10 = 0.9990234375. As normal: 0.9990234375 = 1.998046875·2^-1 = (2 - 2^-9)·2^-1? 1.998046875 = 2 - 2^-9 ✓. So significand = 2 - 2^-9 = 1.1111111110_2 (fraction 0.1111111110 = mantissa 0b1111111110 = 1022). exp = -1, field = 14. So encode_finite(0, 14, 1022) = 0x3bfe — that's what the RTL produced!

So `below1 = 1 - 2^-W_MANT` = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias - 1, (1 << m0) - 2, fmt). Let me verify for b16 (m0=10): encode_finite(0, 14, 1022) = (1024+1022)·2^(14-25) = 2046·2^-11 = 0.9990234375 ✓ = 1 - 2^-10 ✓.

The RP vector: got 0x3bff, want 0x3c00 (1.0). 0x3bff = exp 14, mantissa 1023 = (1024+1023)·2^-11 = 2047·2^-11 = 0.9995117 = 1 - 2^-11. So the RTL rounded up but only to 1 - 2^-11, not all the way to 1.0.

Wait — RP should round toward +inf, so 1/(1+2^-m) = 1 - 2^-m + 2^-2m ≈ 0.9990+ should round UP to 1.0. But the RTL gave 0x3bff = 1 - 2^-11 = 0.9995117, which is BELOW 1.0 but ABOVE 1-2^-10.

Hmm. So the RTL's rounding is off. The exact value = 1/(1+2^-10) = 1 - 2^-10 + 2^-20 - ... = 0.9990234375 + 0.0000009536... = 0.99902439.

The result significand grid: the result is in [0.5, 1), leading exponent -1. ulp = 2^-11. 0.99902439/2^-11 = 2046.0 + 0.99996... wait: 0.99902439·2^11 = 2045.99... let me compute: 0.99902439 × 2048 = 2045.9999... hmm. 1-2^-10 = 0.9990234375. ×2048 = 2046.0000. And the value is slightly above 1-2^-10 → ×2048 = 2046 + tiny. So the significand (in units of 2^-11) is 2046 + tiny.

The RTL placed the quotient with MSB at TARGET. The significand bits: sig = ...2046 ulps (of 2^-11). Rounding: for RP (positive, round toward +inf), round_up = ~rsign & inexact = 1 (inexact). sig + 1 = 2047 → 0x3bff (mantissa 1023 = 2047 - 1024). But that's only 1 - 2^-11, not 1.0!

The issue: rounding up 2046 → 2047 is correct IF the exact value is < 2047 ulps. The exact value = 2046 + 2^-10·2^11·... hmm: 2^-20 in units of 2^-11 = 2^-9. So exact value = 2046 + 2^-9 ulps ≈ 2046.002. Rounding up to the next grid point = 2047 (1 - 2^-11). 

But WAIT — the exact value 0.99902439, rounded up (toward +inf) should be... 1.0! Because the next representable value above 0.99902439 in this format is... the grid is 2^-11 (values below 1 are at exponent -1, ulp 2^-11). The values near 1 are: 0.9990234375 (2046·2^-11 = 1-2^-10), 0.9995117 (2047·2^-11), 1.0 (exp 0). The value 0.99902439 is between 2046 and 2047 (in 2^-11 units) → rounds up to 2047·2^-11 = 0.9995117. But that's not 1.0!

Hmm, but I claimed RP should give 1.0. Let me reconsider. RP rounds toward +inf → the result is the smallest representable value ≥ the exact result. The exact result = 0.99902439. The smallest representable ≥ 0.99902439 is 0.9995117 (2047·2^-11). NOT 1.0!

So the RTL (0x3bff = 0.9995117) is CORRECT, and my expected (1.0) was WRONG.

Wait, let me recheck: is the exact value really only slightly above 1-2^-10? 1/(1+2^-10) = 1 - 2^-10 + 2^-20 - 2^-30 + ... = 0.9990234375 + 0.000000953674... = 0.9990243912. So the smallest representable ≥ value is 0.9995117 ✓. So RTL correct, my expectation wrong.

I confused myself: I thought 1/(1+2^-m) rounds to 1-2^-m (down) or 1 (up), but actually it rounds to 1-2^-m (down) or 1-2^-(m+1) (up), because the value is only 2^-2m above 1-2^-m, and the up-grid-point is 2^-(m+1) away, not 1.

Wait no — hold on. The value 0.9990244 in ulp units (2^-11): 2046.002. Up → 2047. Down → 2046. 2047·2^-11 = 1 - 2^-11. So RP → 2047 → 1-2^-11 ✓ = 0x3bff. That's what RTL gave.

# IEEE 754-2019 floating-point unit (SystemVerilog) with cocotb verification

Parametrized combinational FPU: `W_EXP` exponent bits and `W_MANT` fraction
bits (IEEE 754-2019 3.7 "extendable precision"; binary16/32/64 and odd sizes
are covered by the test matrix). Currently implements addition/subtraction,
multiplication and division (5.4.1) with all five rounding-direction
attributes (4.3), full subnormal support (3.3) and the five exception flags
(7.2-7.6, including divide-by-zero 7.3). Square root, FMA and min/max are
planned milestones.

## Layout

    rtl/                fp_pkg.sv, fp_add.sv, fp_mul.sv, fp_div.sv,
                        fp_add_e8m0.sv, fp_mul_e8m0.sv, fp_div_e8m0.sv,

    tests/reference/    bit-exact Python oracle (exact rational arithmetic)
    tests/test_fp_unit.py     cocotb tests (directed vectors + randomized)
    tests/run_regression.py   builds and runs the width matrix
    tests/exhaustive.py       exhaustive all-vectors sweep of every 8-bit format

input.newString:
## Semantics (bit-exact vs tests/reference)

- NaN results: quiet NaN, sign 0, payload of the first NaN operand (6.2.3).
- Infinity (add): like-sign infinities sum to infinity; magnitude subtraction
  of infinities signals invalid (7.2d). Infinity (mul): the sign of a product
  of infinities is the XOR of the operand signs; inf x 0 signals invalid
  (7.2e). Infinity (div): inf / finite = inf and finite / inf = 0 (sign XOR);
  inf / inf signals invalid (7.2f).
- Zero (add): x + 0 = x; exact zero sums keep the like-sign operand sign,
  else +0 or -0 under roundTowardNegative (6.3). Zero (mul): the sign of a
  product of zeros is the XOR of the operand signs (6.3). Zero (div): 0 / x =
  0 and x / 0 = inf (7.3 divide-by-zero), both with the XOR sign; 0 / 0
  signals invalid (7.2f).
- Overflow (7.4): flagged iff the unbounded-range rounded result exceeds the
  largest finite; RNE/RNA -> inf, RZ -> max finite, RP/RM by sign; inexact
  always set.
- Underflow (7.5): tininess detected after rounding; flagged iff the rounded
  result is a non-zero subnormal and the rounding is inexact. (For add/sub
  the exact result is always a multiple of the minimum subnormal, so the
  flag can never be raised there; mul and div raise it for tiny results.)

## Semantics (bit-exact vs tests/reference)

- NaN results: quiet NaN, sign 0, payload of the first NaN operand (6.2.3).
- Infinity (add): like-sign infinities sum to infinity; magnitude subtraction
  of infinities signals invalid (7.2d). Infinity (mul): the sign of a product
  of infinities is the XOR of the operand signs; inf x 0 signals invalid
  (7.2e).
- Zero (add): x + 0 = x; exact zero sums keep the like-sign operand sign,
  else +0 or -0 under roundTowardNegative (6.3). Zero (mul): the sign of a
  product of zeros is the XOR of the operand signs (6.3); no
  roundTowardNegative sign quirk.
- Overflow (7.4): flagged iff the unbounded-range rounded result exceeds the
  largest finite; RNE/RNA -> inf, RZ -> max finite, RP/RM by sign; inexact
  always set.
- Underflow (7.5): tininess detected after rounding; flagged iff the rounded
  result is a non-zero subnormal and the rounding is inexact. (For add/sub
  the exact result is always a multiple of the minimum subnormal, so the
  flag can never be raised there; mul raises it for subnormal products.)

input.newString:
## FPU features (current state)

### Implemented (M1: add/sub, M2: multiply, M3: division)

- **Operation**: addition, subtraction, multiplication and division (5.4.1).
  `OP_SUB` is `OP_ADD` with the second operand's effective sign flipped.
  `op_t` has `OP_ADD`/`OP_SUB`/`OP_MUL`/`OP_DIV`; `fp_unit.sv` muxes the
  result on `mode == OP_MUL` / `mode == OP_DIV`, defaulting to the add
  datapaths.
- **Parameterized format**: `W_EXP` exponent bits + `W_MANT` fraction bits,
  any width (verified 8-bit family through binary64). Significand is
  `1 + W_MANT` bits, implicit bit (3.3/3.7).
- **Microscaling formats** (`W_MANT = 0`): dedicated `fp_add_e8m0` /
  `fp_mul_e8m0` / `fp_div_e8m0` datapaths for shared-exponent formats
  (E8M0, E7M0, …) with `p = 1` semantics.
- **All five rounding-direction attributes** (4.3): RNE, RNA, RZ, RP, RM.
- **Full subnormal support** (3.3): subnormal operands, subnormal results,
  tininess-after-rounding underflow detection (7.5). For multiply and divide,
  a tiny result (e.g. two subnormals multiplied, or a tiny dividend divided
  by a large divisor) can underflow; for E8M0 (W_MANT = 0) underflow is never
  signaled because the rounded result is either zero or the (non-tiny)
  smallest normal number.
- **Special values** (6.x): qNaN/sNaN (invalid signaling, quiet bit, payload
  of the first NaN operand), infinities (7.2d magnitude-subtraction → invalid
  for add; 7.2e inf × 0 → invalid for mul; 7.2f inf/inf and 0/0 → invalid
  for div), ±0 with clause 6.3 sign rules (products and quotients use the XOR
  of the operand signs), exact cancellation → ±0 per rounding mode (add only).
- **Division by zero** (7.3): finite-nonzero / 0 → ±inf with `FLAG_DIV0`
  signaled (the flag was reserved for this op and is now live). 0/0 is
  invalid (7.2f), not divide-by-zero.
- **Exception flags** (7): invalid, div-by-zero, overflow, underflow, inexact
  are all signaled.
- **Overflow semantics** (7.4): rounded-unbounded-result detection; RNE/RNA →
  ±inf, RZ → ±max finite, RP/RM → ±inf or ±max finite by sign; inexact always
  accompanies overflow. The mul/div datapaths also handle the degenerate
  exponent-range corner (W_EXP = 1, EMIN > EMAX): a subnormal result that
  rounds up to the smallest normal 2^emin, which already exceeds the largest
  finite, signals overflow per 7.4.

### Missing (future milestones)

- **M4 square root** — digit-by-digit with remainder→sticky.
- **M5 FMA + min/max** — fused multiply-add (wide accumulator, single
  rounding); min/max per 5.6.1.
- **M6 comparisons, roundToIntegral, totalOrder** (optional).
- **Microarchitecture**: the datapath is combinational (single `always_comb`
  block, no clock/pipeline). Pipelining, a clocked register interface, and a
  wider opcode space (`op_t`) would be needed for more operations and higher
  throughput.

  exponent-range corner (W_EXP = 1, EMIN > EMAX): a subnormal product that
  rounds up to the smallest normal 2^emin, which already exceeds the largest
  finite, signals overflow per 7.4.

  rounding); min/max per 5.6.1.

## What works (regression-verified)

### Add/sub/mul/div milestone — all 8 widths pass 8/8 test suites

| W_EXP | W_MANT | Format       | Dir | DirMul | DirDiv | Random | MulRnd | DivRnd | Cancel | Boundary |
|-------|--------|--------------|-----|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|----------|
| 4     | 3      | F8 E4M3      | P   | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P        |
| 5     | 10     | binary16     | P   | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P        |
| 8     | 23     | binary32     | P   | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P        |
| 11    | 52     | binary64     | P   | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P        |
| 6     | 16     | odd          | P   | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P        |
| 10    | 40     | odd          | P   | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P        |
| 8     | 0      | F8 E8M0      | P   | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P        |
| 8     | 7      | BF16         | P   | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P        |

All widths pass the full randomized regression at `FP_ITERS=100` (binary64
also at `FP_ITERS=1500`).

### Exhaustive 8-bit verification (add/sub/mul/div)

Every `(op, rm, a, b)` combination — op ∈ {add, sub, mul, div}, all five
rounding modes, all 2^8 values per operand — is checked against the reference
oracle for each of the **7 eight-bit formats** (1+W_EXP+W_MANT == 8):

| W_EXP | W_MANT | Format                | Vectors    | Result |
|-------|--------|-----------------------|------------|--------|
| 1     | 6      | (p=7, emax=0)         | 1,310,720  | PASS   |
| 2     | 5      | (p=6)                 | 1,310,720  | PASS   |
| 3     | 4      | (p=5)                 | 1,310,720  | PASS   |
| 4     | 3      | F8 E4M3               | 1,310,720  | PASS   |
| 5     | 2      | F8 E5M2               | 1,310,720  | PASS   |
| 6     | 1      | (p=2)                 | 1,310,720  | PASS   |
| 7     | 0      | E7M0 microscaling     | 1,310,720  | PASS   |

**9,175,040 vectors total, 0 mismatches.** The harness is a standalone
Verilator C++ driver (`tests/exhaustive_main.cpp`) driven by
`tests/exhaustive.py`, which precomputes the expected results with
`tests/reference/ops.py`. It bypasses cocotb entirely, so the whole sweep runs
in ~2-3 min. Since the datapath is identical at every width, exhaustive
coverage of the 8-bit family gives high confidence for the larger formats too.
Note the harness caches its binary and expected files: after RTL/reference
changes run `FORCE_REBUILD=1` and delete stale `exhaustive_build/*/expected.bin`
(the binary fails with "truncated expected file" if they are out of sync).

Index: HANDOFF.md
===================================================================
--- HANDOFF.md	
+++ HANDOFF.md	
@@ -1,370 +1,394 @@
 # FP Unit — Handoff Report
 
 ## Project
 
 IEEE 754-2019 floating-point unit in SystemVerilog, verified against a
 bit-exact Python oracle (exact rational arithmetic, clause 4.3 rounding) via
 cocotb randomized regression plus exhaustive all-vector checks of every 8-bit
 format.
 
 ## Toolchain (pinned, per user instruction)
 
 - **Verilator 5.020** (Debian system package `/usr/bin/verilator`)
 - **cocotb 1.9.2** (`pyproject.toml` pins `cocotb>=1.9.2,<2`; cocotb 2.x
   requires Verilator ≥5.036 which is not available)
 - **Python 3.13** (uv-managed, `.venv`)
 - **uv** for dependency management (`uv sync`, `uv run`)
 
 ### Toolchain quirks (workarounds in place)
 
 1. **cocotb 1.9.2's `verilator.cpp` does not advance Verilator's internal
    clock.** Without the patch, every `await Timer(1, "ns")` stalls for ~2
    seconds. `tests/run_regression.py` patches the venv's
    `cocotb/share/lib/verilator/verilator.cpp` on every run (idempotent):
    adds `Verilated::time(main_time);` after `main_time = next_time;`.
    The patch bumps the file mtime by 2 seconds to force `make` to recompile
    `verilator.o` (avoids the equal-mtime pitfall).
 
 2. **The sim occasionally hangs at startup** (cocotb 1.9.2 + Verilator 5.020
    race). `run_regression.py` retries each width up to 3 times on timeout
    (default 1800 s per attempt).
 
 3. **`pkill -f "path/fp_unit"` kills its own shell** (the pattern matches the
    shell's command line). Use `kill -9 $(pgrep -x fp_unit)` instead.
 
 > Former quirk: the sim used to take ~2 s/transaction, blamed on cocotb's VPI
 > overhead. This turned out to be an RTL bug (bug 14 below): a subnormal-path
 > loop ran 2^32 iterations per normal-path transaction. Fixed — the full
 > 8-width regression now runs in ~1 s.
 
 ## Repository layout
 
 ```
 rtl/
   fp_pkg.sv           Package: rounding-mode/opcode enums, flag bit positions
   fp_add.sv           Generic add/sub (W_MANT > 0): align → GRS add → round
   fp_mul.sv           Generic mul (W_MANT > 0): 2p-bit product → place → round
+  fp_div.sv           Generic div (W_MANT > 0): long division → place → round
   fp_add_e8m0.sv      Dedicated E8M0 add/sub (W_MANT = 0): power-of-two logic
   fp_mul_e8m0.sv      Dedicated E8M0 mul (W_MANT = 0): exact 2^(e_a+e_b) logic
+  fp_div_e8m0.sv      Dedicated E8M0 div (W_MANT = 0): exact 2^(e_a-e_b) logic
   fp_unit.sv          Top: generate-switch between the *_e8m0 and generic ops
 tests/
   reference/
     formats.py        BinFormat dataclass, encode/decode/classify
     rounding.py       round_to_format (exact rational → bits + flags)
-    ops.py            fp_add/fp_mul reference (special cases + rounding)
+    ops.py            fp_add/fp_mul/fp_div reference (specials + rounding)
     gen.py            Random input generators (uniform, boundary, subnormal…)
   test_fp_unit.py     Cocotb tests: directed vectors + randomized regression
   run_regression.py   Build + run loop with timeout/retry, self-patching
   exhaustive_main.cpp Standalone Verilator C++ harness (fast all-vectors check)
   exhaustive.py       Driver: reference expected vectors + build/run exhaustive
 Makefile              Convenience targets: regress, regress-all, smoke, lint
 pyproject.toml        cocotb>=1.9.2,<2 dependency
 README.md             Usage and semantics documentation
 ```
 
 Build artifacts (`sim_build/`, `exhaustive_build/`, `obj_dir/`) and the
 vendored `cocotb/`/`verilator/` source trees are gitignored.
 
 ## FPU features (current state)
 
 ### Implemented (M1: add/sub, M2: multiply, M3: division)
 
 - **Operation**: addition, subtraction, multiplication and division (5.4.1).
   `OP_SUB` is `OP_ADD` with the second operand's effective sign flipped.
   `op_t` has `OP_ADD`/`OP_SUB`/`OP_MUL`/`OP_DIV`; `fp_unit.sv` muxes the
   result on `mode == OP_MUL` / `mode == OP_DIV`, defaulting to the add
   datapaths.
 - **Parameterized format**: `W_EXP` exponent bits + `W_MANT` fraction bits,
   any width (verified 8-bit family through binary64). Significand is
   `1 + W_MANT` bits, implicit bit (3.3/3.7).
 - **Microscaling formats** (`W_MANT = 0`): dedicated `fp_add_e8m0` /
   `fp_mul_e8m0` / `fp_div_e8m0` datapaths for shared-exponent formats
   (E8M0, E7M0, …) with `p = 1` semantics.
 - **All five rounding-direction attributes** (4.3): RNE, RNA, RZ, RP, RM.
 - **Full subnormal support** (3.3): subnormal operands, subnormal results,
   tininess-after-rounding underflow detection (7.5). For multiply and divide,
   a tiny result (e.g. two subnormals multiplied, or a tiny dividend divided
   by a large divisor) can underflow; for E8M0 (W_MANT = 0) underflow is never
   signaled because the rounded result is either zero or the (non-tiny)
   smallest normal number.
 - **Special values** (6.x): qNaN/sNaN (invalid signaling, quiet bit, payload
   of the first NaN operand), infinities (7.2d magnitude-subtraction → invalid
   for add; 7.2e inf × 0 → invalid for mul; 7.2f inf/inf and 0/0 → invalid
   for div), ±0 with clause 6.3 sign rules (products and quotients use the XOR
   of the operand signs), exact cancellation → ±0 per rounding mode (add only).
 - **Division by zero** (7.3): finite-nonzero / 0 → ±inf with `FLAG_DIV0`
   signaled (the flag was reserved for this op and is now live). 0/0 is
   invalid (7.2f), not divide-by-zero.
 - **Exception flags** (7): invalid, div-by-zero, overflow, underflow, inexact
   are all signaled.
 - **Overflow semantics** (7.4): rounded-unbounded-result detection; RNE/RNA →
   ±inf, RZ → ±max finite, RP/RM → ±inf or ±max finite by sign; inexact always
   accompanies overflow. The mul/div datapaths also handle the degenerate
   exponent-range corner (W_EXP = 1, EMIN > EMAX): a subnormal result that
   rounds up to the smallest normal 2^emin, which already exceeds the largest
   finite, signals overflow per 7.4.
 
 ### Missing (future milestones)
 
 - **M4 square root** — digit-by-digit with remainder→sticky.
 - **M5 FMA + min/max** — fused multiply-add (wide accumulator, single
   rounding); min/max per 5.6.1.
 - **M6 comparisons, roundToIntegral, totalOrder** (optional).
 - **Microarchitecture**: the datapath is combinational (single `always_comb`
   block, no clock/pipeline). Pipelining, a clocked register interface, and a
   wider opcode space (`op_t`) would be needed for more operations and higher
   throughput.
 
 ## What works (regression-verified)
 
 ### Add/sub/mul/div milestone — all 8 widths pass 8/8 test suites
 
 | W_EXP | W_MANT | Format       | Dir | DirMul | DirDiv | Random | MulRnd | DivRnd | Cancel | Boundary |
 |-------|--------|--------------|-----|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|--------|----------|
 | 4     | 3      | F8 E4M3      | P   | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P        |
 | 5     | 10     | binary16     | P   | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P        |
 | 8     | 23     | binary32     | P   | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P        |
 | 11    | 52     | binary64     | P   | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P        |
 | 6     | 16     | odd          | P   | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P        |
 | 10    | 40     | odd          | P   | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P        |
 | 8     | 0      | F8 E8M0      | P   | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P        |
 | 8     | 7      | BF16         | P   | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P      | P        |
 
 All widths pass the full randomized regression at `FP_ITERS=100` (binary64
 also at `FP_ITERS=1500`).
 
 ### Exhaustive 8-bit verification (add/sub/mul/div)
 
 Every `(op, rm, a, b)` combination — op ∈ {add, sub, mul, div}, all five
 rounding modes, all 2^8 values per operand — is checked against the reference
 oracle for each of the **7 eight-bit formats** (1+W_EXP+W_MANT == 8):
 
 | W_EXP | W_MANT | Format                | Vectors    | Result |
 |-------|--------|-----------------------|------------|--------|
 | 1     | 6      | (p=7, emax=0)         | 1,310,720  | PASS   |
 | 2     | 5      | (p=6)                 | 1,310,720  | PASS   |
 | 3     | 4      | (p=5)                 | 1,310,720  | PASS   |
 | 4     | 3      | F8 E4M3               | 1,310,720  | PASS   |
 | 5     | 2      | F8 E5M2               | 1,310,720  | PASS   |
 | 6     | 1      | (p=2)                 | 1,310,720  | PASS   |
 | 7     | 0      | E7M0 microscaling     | 1,310,720  | PASS   |
 
 **9,175,040 vectors total, 0 mismatches.** The harness is a standalone
 Verilator C++ driver (`tests/exhaustive_main.cpp`) driven by
 `tests/exhaustive.py`, which precomputes the expected results with
 `tests/reference/ops.py`. It bypasses cocotb entirely, so the whole sweep runs
 in ~2-3 min. Since the datapath is identical at every width, exhaustive
 coverage of the 8-bit family gives high confidence for the larger formats too.
 Note the harness caches its binary and expected files: after RTL/reference
 changes run `FORCE_REBUILD=1` and delete stale `exhaustive_build/*/expected.bin`
 (the binary fails with "truncated expected file" if they are out of sync).
 
 ## Bugs found and fixed during development
 
 1. **`$signed(a_exp)` misread exponent fields ≥ 2^(W_EXP-1)** as negative.
    Fix: plain `a_exp - BIAS` (unsigned field promoted by signed 32-bit BIAS).
 
 2. **Off-by-one size cast** `(W_EXP+2)'(...)` truncated the sign bit of
    `e_a`/`e_b`. Fix: cast to `(W_EXP+3)` bits.
 
 3. **Alignment sticky never propagated** into `norm_sticky`. Fix: initialize
    `norm_sticky = align_sticky` at the top of the normalize block.
 
 4. **Effective-subtraction sticky sign** — for opposite-sign adds, the
    alignment sticky must be *subtracted* (borrowed), not added. Fix: `mag =
    mag - 1` when `diff_sticky` is set (complement trick for GRS).
 
 5. **Bogus sticky loop in left-normalize** — the loop `for (i < TARGET-p0)
    norm_sticky |= mag[i]` ORed the leading bit into the sticky. Fix: removed
    the loop (left-normalize loses no bits; the field is wide enough).
 
 6. **`QUIET` 32-bit overflow** for W_MANT ≥ 32 (binary64). Fix: sized
    `localparam logic [MANT_W-1:0] QUIET = (MANT_W)'(1) << (MANT_W - 1)`.
 
 7. **Reference-model RM rounding bug** — `_round_up` returned `True`
    unconditionally for `MODE_RM` regardless of sign. Fix: `return sign == 1`.
 
 8. **Verilator 5.020 V3Gate internal fault at W_MANT = 0** — gate optimizer
    crashes on the generic datapath's subnormal block at 1-bit widths. Fix:
    dedicated `fp_add_e8m0.sv` module for W_MANT = 0, selected via `generate`
    in `fp_unit.sv`.
 
 9. **Verilator 5.020 parse limitation** — replications with non-literal
    counts cannot appear as first/middle items in a concatenation. Fix:
    replaced `{(S_W-MANT_W){1'b1}, a_mant}` with `((S_W)'(1'b1) << W_MANT) |
    {1'b0, a_mant}`.
 
 10. **Verilator equal-mtime pitfall** — patching `verilator.cpp` in the same
     second as the build caused `make` to skip recompilation. Fix: bump mtime
     by 2 seconds in the patch function.
 
 11. **`gen.py` negative shift at W_MANT = 0** — `_mantissa(extreme=True)`
     computed `1 << (W_MANT - 1)`, raising `ValueError: negative shift count`
     in the random/boundary tests for E8M0. Fix: early `return 0` when
     `fmt.W_MANT == 0` (the only mantissa value is 0).
 
 12. **E8M0 RP/RM rounding was sign-blind** — the `up` (round up to the larger
     magnitude) decisions in the same-sign d1/d2p and opposite-sign d2p cases
     treated RP/RM like RNE. RM of a negative result therefore rounded toward
     zero instead of −∞ (e.g. `-2^-50 + -2^-60` under RM gave `-2^-50` instead
     of `-2^-51`). Fix: `RP -> up iff rsign == 0`, `RM -> up iff rsign == 1`
     in all three rounding-decision sites of `fp_add_e8m0.sv`.

     exponent difference 1 gives the exact value `2^e_min` with the sign of the
     larger-magnitude operand, but `rsign` defaulted to `a_sign` (e.g.
     `2^-26 - 2^-25` gave `+2^-26` instead of `-2^-26`). Fix: `rsign = (e_a >=
     e_b) ? a_sign : b_sign_eff` in the d1 branch.
 
 14. **Subnormal block `int unsigned shift` → 2^32-iteration loop** — the
     subnormal `always_comb` evaluates for every input, but its outputs are
     only selected when `e_res < EMIN`. `shift = EMIN - e_res` goes negative
     for a normal result and, as `int unsigned`, wraps to ~4.3 billion; the
     sticky loop `for (i < shift)` then iterated 2^32 times per normal-path
     transaction. This was the real cause of the "~2 s/transaction" slowness
     (not cocotb VPI overhead, as previously assumed). Fix: `int signed shift`
     plus a `shift > 0` guard. The full 8-width regression dropped from ~1 h
     to ~1 s.
 
 15. **M2: product-exponent carry missing** — `e_res = e_a + e_b` was off by
     one whenever the significand product carried out of its own grid
     (`bitlen(P) == bitlen(s_a) + bitlen(s_b)`, i.e. two normal significands
     whose product is ≥ 2^(2·S_W-1)). Found by the binary16 regression
     (e.g. `-3.328 × 1002` came out as `-1667` instead of `-3334`). Fix:
     `e_res = e_a + e_b + (pbitlen(P) == bitlen(s_a) + bitlen(s_b))` in
     `fp_mul.sv`.

     the degenerate W_EXP = 1 range (EMIN = 1 > EMAX = 0, where every finite
     value is a subnormal and the smallest normal 2^emin = 2 already exceeds
     max finite 1.984), a subnormal product rounding up to the min normal must
     signal overflow per 7.4. Found by the exhaustive (1,6) sweep (80
     vectors, e.g. `1.031 × 1.9375 → 2`, flags `0x01` vs want `0x05`). The
     carry of the p-bit unbounded rounding is detected on the subnormal grid:
     RNE/RNA need guard+round (`gs & rs`), RP/RM (which round up for any
     inexact, by sign) need just the guard bit. Fix: an overflow
     saturation branch in the subnormal path's "round up to min normal" case
     when `EMIN > EMAX` (constant-false for all non-degenerate formats).

     RTL) — `(1+2^-m)^2 → 1+2^-(m-1)` is mantissa `2`, not `1 << (m-1)`;
     RP rounds a positive inexact result up (mantissa 3); `max sub × 2`
     encodes as `encode_finite(0, 1, maxm-1)` and is subnormal-only (E8M0 has
     no subnormals); the E8M0 half-2^emin tie needs `e_a + e_b = emin - 1`
     with `e_b = e_a - 1` (not `-2`).

+    sweep on its first run.** The only fixes were test/reference-side:
+    - `1/(1+2^-m)`: on the [0.5,1) grid the value is `2^m - 2 + 2^-m` ulps,
+      so RP rounds up to `1 - 2^-(m+1)`, not 1.0; the "below 1" encoding is
+      `encode_finite(0, bias-1, 2^m - 2)`, not `(bias, 2^m - 1)` (which is
+      `2 - 2^-m`).

+      `0x3F2AAAAB`); the generic `1/3` vector depends on `W_MANT` parity and
+      was replaced by the `1/(1+2^-m)` family.
+    - E8M0 division tie exponents: `e_a - e_b = emin - 1` with `e_b = e_a +
+      emax` (not `+ emax + 1`).
+    - The NaN directed vectors are meaningless for E8M0 (no NaN encodings)
+      and the `div_close` pair generator shifted by `W_MANT-1` (guarded for
+      `W_MANT = 0`).

+    `e_res = e_a - e_b - (a_al < b_al)`, remainder → sticky) matched the
+    oracle across all 9,175,040 exhaustive vectors.

 ## Format-specific notes
 
 ### E8M0 (W_MANT = 0, 1 sign + W_EXP exponent + 0 mantissa)
 
 - IEEE 754-2025 microscaling shared-exponent format (all finite values are
   exact powers of two; no subnormals, no NaN encodings).
 - `p = 1` tie rule (4.3.1): both candidates have significand 1.0 (odd), so
   `roundTiesToEven` delivers the larger magnitude. Implemented explicitly in
   `fp_add_e8m0.sv`.
 - Rounding-direction handling for RP/RM is sign-dependent (see bug 12), and
   the opposite-sign d1 subtraction sign is fixed (bug 13); both were found by
   the E8M0 sim, which had never been run before.
-- Invalid (inf + -inf, inf × 0) → +infinity (no NaN encoding exists);
-  documented in the modules and the reference (`encode_nan` returns
+- Invalid (inf + -inf, inf × 0, inf/inf, 0/0) → +infinity (no NaN encoding
+  exists); documented in the modules and the reference (`encode_nan` returns
   `encode_inf(0, fmt)` when `W_MANT == 0`).
 - **Multiplication** (`fp_mul_e8m0.sv`): the product 2^e_a × 2^e_b = 2^(e_a+e_b)
   is exact, but may leave the exponent range. Overflow (e_a+e_b > emax)
   saturates per attribute with overflow+inexact. Tiny results (e_a+e_b < emin)
   round to 0 or 2^emin with inexact only — underflow is never signaled
   (tininess after rounding; the rounded result is zero or the non-tiny
   smallest normal). The only tie is the exact value 2^(emin-1): RNE → 0
   (significand 0 even), RNA → 2^emin, RP/RM by sign.
+- **Division** (`fp_div_e8m0.sv`): the quotient 2^e_a / 2^e_b = 2^(e_a-e_b)
+  is exact, with the same overflow/tiny/rounding behavior as multiplication
+  (the tie is again 2^(emin-1) with e_a - e_b = emin - 1). Division by zero
+  (finite / 0) returns infinity with the divide-by-zero flag (7.3);
+  0/0 and inf/inf are invalid (7.2f) → +infinity.
 - `fp_add_e8m0.sv` has `/* verilator lint_off WIDTHEXPAND */` and
   `WIDTHTRUNC` (same as `fp_add.sv`) — int/width mixing in exponent
   arithmetic.

   `fp_add` handles it. Sim-verified (4/4).

 ```bash

 # Single width
 ```

input.newString:
- Invalid (inf + -inf, inf × 0, inf/inf, 0/0) → +infinity (no NaN encoding
  exists); documented in the modules and the reference (`encode_nan` returns
  `encode_inf(0, fmt)` when `W_MANT == 0`).
- **Multiplication** (`fp_mul_e8m0.sv`): the product 2^e_a × 2^e_b = 2^(e_a+e_b)
  is exact, but may leave the exponent range. Overflow (e_a+e_b > emax)
  saturates per attribute with overflow+inexact. Tiny results (e_a+e_b < emin)
  round to 0 or 2^emin with inexact only — underflow is never signaled
  (tininess after rounding; the rounded result is zero or the non-tiny
  smallest normal). The only tie is the exact value 2^(emin-1): RNE → 0
  (significand 0 even), RNA → 2^emin, RP/RM by sign.
- **Division** (`fp_div_e8m0.sv`): the quotient 2^e_a / 2^e_b = 2^(e_a-e_b)
  is exact, with the same overflow/tiny/rounding behavior as multiplication
  (the tie is again 2^(emin-1) with e_a - e_b = emin - 1). Division by zero
  (finite / 0) returns infinity with the divide-by-zero flag (7.3);
  0/0 and inf/inf are invalid (7.2f) → +infinity.

M3 (IEEE 754 division) is implemented and fully verified.

## What was done

**RTL**
- `fp_pkg.sv`: added `OP_DIV = 3'd3`; `FLAG_DIV0` is now live.
- `fp_div.sv` (new): generic division — aligns both significands to their MSB, does integer long division (`q_raw = (a_al << S_W+2) / b_al`), places the quotient MSB at `TARGET`, and derives `e_res = e_a - e_b - (a_al < b_al)`; the division remainder feeds the sticky. Rounding/overflow/subnormal paths mirror `fp_mul.sv`.
- `fp_div_e8m0.sv` (new): E8M0 division (`2^(e_a-e_b)`, overflow + tiny-rounding to 0/`2^emin`, x/0 → ±inf+div0, 0/0 & inf/inf → invalid).
- `fp_unit.sv`: muxes the div datapath on `mode == OP_DIV`.

**Reference/tests/harness**
- `ops.py`: `fp_div` oracle (7.2f inf/inf & 0/0 invalid, 7.3 finite/0 → div0).
- `gen.py`: `div_close`/`div_extreme` pair styles.
- `test_fp_unit.py`: `test_directed_div` + `test_div_random`; `test_random_mixed` now picks from all 4 ops.
- `run_regression.py`, `exhaustive.py`, `exhaustive_main.cpp`: 4-op sweep.
- `Makefile`, `README.md`, `HANDOFF.md` updated.

## Verification
- `make lint`: clean (-Wall).
- Full 8-width matrix: **8/8 tests per width**, plus binary64 at `FP_ITERS=1500`.
- **Exhaustive: 9,175,040 vectors (4 ops × 5 rm × all 8-bit operands × 7 formats), 0 mismatches.**

## Notable
Unlike add/sub and mul, **the division datapath passed the exhaustive sweep on its first run — no RTL bugs.** All fixes were test-side (documented as bug 18 in HANDOFF): encoding errors for `1-2^-m`/`1/(1+2^-m)`, a `2/3` hex typo, E8M0 tie exponents, and E8M0-incompatible NaN vectors.

Next up per the plan: **M4 square root** (`isqrt`-style digit-by-digit with remainder→sticky).

    replaced `{(S_W-MANT_W){1'b1}, a_mant}` with `((S_W)'(1'b1) << W_MANT) |

     by 2 seconds in the patch function.
 
 11. **`gen.py` negative shift at W_MANT = 0** — `_mantissa(extreme=True)`
     computed `1 << (W_MANT - 1)`, raising `ValueError: negative shift count`
     in the random/boundary tests for E8M0. Fix: early `return 0` when
     `fmt.W_MANT == 0` (the only mantissa value is 0).
 
 12. **E8M0 RP/RM rounding was sign-blind** — the `up` (round up to the larger
     magnitude) decisions in the same-sign d1/d2p and opposite-sign d2p cases
     treated RP/RM like RNE. RM of a negative result therefore rounded toward
     zero instead of −∞ (e.g. `-2^-50 + -2^-60` under RM gave `-2^-50` instead
     of `-2^-51`). Fix: `RP -> up iff rsign == 0`, `RM -> up iff rsign == 1`
     in all three rounding-decision sites of `fp_add_e8m0.sv`.
 
 13. **E8M0 opposite-sign d1 never set `rsign`** — magnitude subtraction with
     exponent difference 1 gives the exact value `2^e_min` with the sign of the
     larger-magnitude operand, but `rsign` defaulted to `a_sign` (e.g.
     `2^-26 - 2^-25` gave `+2^-26` instead of `-2^-26`). Fix: `rsign = (e_a >=
     e_b) ? a_sign : b_sign_eff` in the d1 branch.
 
 14. **Subnormal block `int unsigned shift` → 2^32-iteration loop** — the
     subnormal `always_comb` evaluates for every input, but its outputs are
     only selected when `e_res < EMIN`. `shift = EMIN - e_res` goes negative
     for a normal result and, as `int unsigned`, wraps to ~4.3 billion; the
     sticky loop `for (i < shift)` then iterated 2^32 times per normal-path
     transaction. This was the real cause of the "~2 s/transaction" slowness
     (not cocotb VPI overhead, as previously assumed). Fix: `int signed shift`
     plus a `shift > 0` guard. The full 8-width regression dropped from ~1 h
     to ~1 s.
 
 15. **M2: product-exponent carry missing** — `e_res = e_a + e_b` was off by
     one whenever the significand product carried out of its own grid
     (`bitlen(P) == bitlen(s_a) + bitlen(s_b)`, i.e. two normal significands
     whose product is ≥ 2^(2·S_W-1)). Found by the binary16 regression
     (e.g. `-3.328 × 1002` came out as `-1667` instead of `-3334`). Fix:
     `e_res = e_a + e_b + (pbitlen(P) == bitlen(s_a) + bitlen(s_b))` in
     `fp_mul.sv`.
 
 16. **M2: subnormal round-up past the largest finite never overflowed** — for
     the degenerate W_EXP = 1 range (EMIN = 1 > EMAX = 0, where every finite
     value is a subnormal and the smallest normal 2^emin = 2 already exceeds
     max finite 1.984), a subnormal product rounding up to the min normal must
     signal overflow per 7.4. Found by the exhaustive (1,6) sweep (80
     vectors, e.g. `1.031 × 1.9375 → 2`, flags `0x01` vs want `0x05`). The
     carry of the p-bit unbounded rounding is detected on the subnormal grid:
     RNE/RNA need guard+round (`gs & rs`), RP/RM (which round up for any
     inexact, by sign) need just the guard bit. Fix: an overflow
     saturation branch in the subnormal path's "round up to min normal" case
     when `EMIN > EMAX` (constant-false for all non-degenerate formats).

     RTL) — `(1+2^-m)^2 → 1+2^-(m-1)` is mantissa `2`, not `1 << (m-1)`;

     encodes as `encode_finite(0, 1, maxm-1)` and is subnormal-only (E8M0 has
     no subnormals); the E8M0 half-2^emin tie needs `e_a + e_b = emin - 1`
     with `e_b = e_a - 1` (not `-2`).

 # IEEE 754-2019 floating-point unit (SystemVerilog) with cocotb verification
 
 Parametrized combinational FPU: `W_EXP` exponent bits and `W_MANT` fraction
 bits (IEEE 754-2019 3.7 "extendable precision"; binary16/32/64 and odd sizes
 are covered by the test matrix). Currently implements addition/subtraction,
-multiplication and division (5.4.1) with all five rounding-direction

-planned milestones.

+rounding-direction attributes (4.3), full subnormal support (3.3) and the
+five exception flags (7.2-7.6, including divide-by-zero 7.3). FMA and
+min/max are planned milestones.

-    rtl/                fp_pkg.sv, fp_add.sv, fp_mul.sv, fp_div.sv,
+    rtl/                fp_pkg.sv, fp_add.sv, fp_mul.sv, fp_div.sv, fp_sqrt.sv,

-                        fp_unit.sv (synthesizable SV)
+                        fp_sqrt_e8m0.sv, fp_unit.sv (synthesizable SV)

     tests/test_fp_unit.py     cocotb tests (directed vectors + randomized)
     tests/run_regression.py   builds and runs the width matrix
     tests/exhaustive.py       exhaustive all-vectors sweep of every 8-bit format
 
 ## Running
 
     uv run python tests/run_regression.py            # default matrix
     uv run python tests/run_regression.py --all      # full 8-width matrix
     uv run python tests/run_regression.py --width 8 23
     FP_ITERS=200 uv run python tests/run_regression.py --width 8 23
     uv run python tests/exhaustive.py                # ~1 min, 7 formats x 3 ops
     make regress | make smoke | make lint
 
 ## Toolchain notes
 
 - System Verilator is 5.020 (Debian), which requires cocotb < 2 (cocotb 2.x
   needs Verilator >= 5.036); pyproject pins `cocotb>=1.9.2,<2`.
 - `tests/run_regression.py` patches cocotb 1.9.2's `verilator.cpp` on first
   run: it adds `Verilated::time(main_time)` so Verilator's internal clock
   advances; without this, every cocotb Timer wait stalls ~2 s and the sim
   occasionally hangs. The patch is idempotent and survives `uv sync`.

   the regression runner retries timed-out widths and detects hangs via a
   per-attempt wall-clock timeout.

   `exhaustive_build/*/expected.bin` files must be removed after changing the
   reference oracle (the binary detects a truncated file and fails loudly).
 
 ## Semantics (bit-exact vs tests/reference)
 
 - NaN results: quiet NaN, sign 0, payload of the first NaN operand (6.2.3).
 - Infinity (add): like-sign infinities sum to infinity; magnitude subtraction
   of infinities signals invalid (7.2d). Infinity (mul): the sign of a product
   of infinities is the XOR of the operand signs; inf x 0 signals invalid
   (7.2e). Infinity (div): inf / finite = inf and finite / inf = 0 (sign XOR);
   inf / inf signals invalid (7.2f).
 - Zero (add): x + 0 = x; exact zero sums keep the like-sign operand sign,
   else +0 or -0 under roundTowardNegative (6.3). Zero (mul): the sign of a
   product of zeros is the XOR of the operand signs (6.3). Zero (div): 0 / x =

+    if a_cls == ZERO:

     import tempfile
 
     with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".log", delete=False) as f:
         log_path = f.name

     verilator.cpp if not already applied.

     Timer wait stalls for the embed's poll interval (~2 s per transaction).
     The venv copy is recreated by `uv sync`, so this runs on every invocation.

     p = Path(sysconfig.get_paths()["purelib"]) / "cocotb" / "share" / "lib" / "verilator" / "verilator.cpp"

     ap.add_argument("--all", action="store_true",
                     help="run the full width matrix (6 widths)")
     ap.add_argument("--tests", default="test_fp_unit",

     ap.add_argument("--retries", type=int, default=3,

     ap.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=1800,

             build_args=["--timing"],

             continue

             else:
                 print(f"    attempt {attempt}: rc={rc} {timing} - retrying", flush=True)
             if attempt >= args.retries:
                 print("    giving up on this width", flush=True)
                 failures += 1
                 break

         print(f"REGRESSION FAILED: {failures} failing tests", flush=True)
         return 1
     print("all widths passed", flush=True)
     return 0

         (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, infs, infs, infs, 0, "-inf + -inf = -inf"),
         (OP_SUB, MODE_RNE, inf, infs, inf, 0, "inf - -inf = inf"),
         (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, inf, infs, qnan, 1 << formats.FLAG_INVALID, "inf + -inf -> qNaN, invalid"),
         (OP_SUB, MODE_RNE, inf, inf, qnan, 1 << formats.FLAG_INVALID, "inf - inf -> qNaN, invalid"),
         (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, inf, m1, inf, 0, "inf + 1 = inf"),
         (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, m1, inf, inf, 0, "1 + inf = inf"),
         (OP_SUB, MODE_RNE, m1, inf, infs, 0, "1 - inf = -inf"),
         (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, qnan, m1, qnan, 0, "qNaN + 1 -> qNaN"),
         (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, m1, qnan, qnan, 0, "1 + qNaN -> qNaN"),
     ]
     if w == 32:
         v += [
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, 0x7FC00001, m1, 0x7FC00001, 0, "qNaN payload passthrough"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, 0x7F800001, m1, 0x7FC00001, 1 << formats.FLAG_INVALID,
              "sNaN -> qNaN, invalid"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, m1, 0xFF80000F, 0x7FC0000F, 1 << formats.FLAG_INVALID,
              "sNaN payload kept, invalid"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, 0x7FC00003, 0x7F800005, 0x7FC00003, 1 << formats.FLAG_INVALID,
              "a NaN wins payload, sNaN -> invalid"),
         ]
 
     # --- basic arithmetic (RNE)
     v += [
         (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, m1, m1, encode_finite(0, fmt.bias + 1, 0, fmt), 0, "1 + 1 = 2"),
         (OP_SUB, MODE_RNE, m1, m1s, encode_finite(0, fmt.bias + 1, 0, fmt), 0, "1 - -1 = 2"),
     ]
     if fmt.W_MANT > 0:
         v += [
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, m1, encode_finite(0, fmt.bias, 1 << (m0 - 1), fmt),
              encode_finite(0, fmt.bias + 1, 1 << (m0 - 2), fmt), 0, "1 + 1.5 = 2.5"),
         ]
     # --- subnormal boundary (generic; all exact, so no flags)
     # Subnormals do not exist for W_MANT = 0 (E8M0).
     if fmt.W_MANT > 0:
         v += [
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, minn, maxsn, encode_finite(0, 1, maxm, fmt), 0,
              "min normal + max subnormal = 2^-125 - 2^-149 (exact)"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, minn, minn, encode_finite(0, 2, 0, fmt), 0, "min normal + min normal"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, minsn, minsn, encode_finite(0, 0, 2, fmt), 0,
              "min subnormal + min subnormal"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, minsn, neg(minsn), z, 0, "subnormal cancellation"),
             (OP_SUB, MODE_RNE, encode_finite(0, 1, 1, fmt), minn, minsn, 0,
              "min normal + ulp - min normal = min subnormal (exact)"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, minn, neg(maxsn), minsn, 0,
              "min normal - max subnormal = min subnormal (exact, no underflow)"),
         ]
     # --- overflow (7.4)
     v += [
         (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, maxf, maxf, inf, 0x05, "max + max -> +inf (RNE)"),
         (OP_ADD, MODE_RZ, maxf, maxf, maxf, 0x05, "max + max -> max (RZ)"),
         (OP_ADD, MODE_RM, maxf, maxf, maxf, 0x05, "max + max -> max (RM, positive)"),
         (OP_ADD, MODE_RP, maxf, maxf, inf, 0x05, "max + max -> +inf (RP)"),
         (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, maxs, maxs, infs, 0x05, "-max + -max -> -inf (RNE)"),
         (OP_ADD, MODE_RP, maxs, maxs, maxs, 0x05, "-max + -max -> -max (RP, negative)"),
         (OP_ADD, MODE_RM, maxs, maxs, infs, 0x05, "-max + -max -> -inf (RM)"),
         (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, maxf, m1, maxf, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "max + 1 -> max, inexact"),
         (OP_ADD, MODE_RP, maxf, m1, inf, 0x05, "max + 1 -> inf under RP, overflow"),
     ]
     if w == 32:
         # Tie at the overflow threshold: exact sum = 2^128 - 2^103 (0x73000000 = 2^103).
         # Per 7.4 the overflow flag tracks the rounded result with unbounded
         # exponent range: RNE/RNA round the tie to 2^128 (> max) -> overflow;
         # RZ/RM round down to max finite exactly -> inexact only.
         v += [
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, maxf, 0x73000000, inf, 0x05, "overflow tie -> inf (RNE even)"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNA, maxf, 0x73000000, inf, 0x05, "overflow tie -> inf (RNA)"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RZ, maxf, 0x73000000, maxf, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT,
              "overflow tie -> max (RZ), inexact only"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RM, maxf, 0x73000000, maxf, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT,
              "overflow tie -> max (RM), inexact only"),
         ]
     # --- E8M0 (W_MANT = 0) ties and exact powers (4.3.1: p = 1 ties -> larger).
     if fmt.W_MANT == 0:
         pe  = maxf                                            # 2^EMAX
         pem = encode_finite(0, fmt.emax - 1 + fmt.bias, 0, fmt)   # 2^(EMAX-1)
         pe2 = encode_finite(0, fmt.emax - 2 + fmt.bias, 0, fmt)   # 2^(EMAX-2)
         pe3 = encode_finite(0, fmt.emax - 3 + fmt.bias, 0, fmt)   # 2^(EMAX-3)
         v += [
             # 2^EMAX + 2^EMAX = 2^(EMAX+1): overflow (rounded-unbounded > max)
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, pe, pe, inf, 0x05, "e8m0: 2^EMAX + 2^EMAX -> inf (RNE, OF)"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RZ,  pe, pe, maxf, 0x05, "e8m0: max + max -> max (RZ, OF+INE)"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RP,  pe, pe, inf, 0x05, "e8m0: max + max -> inf (RP, OF)"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RM,  pe, pe, maxf, 0x05, "e8m0: max + max (pos) -> max (RM, OF+INE)"),
             # Tie: 2^EMAX + 2^(EMAX-1) = 1.5*2^EMAX -> RNE/RNA/RP larger (inf),
             # RZ/RM smaller (max finite, inexact only: rounded-unbounded = max).
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, pe, pem, inf, 0x05, "e8m0: tie -> +inf (RNE, OF)"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RZ,  pe, pem, maxf, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "e8m0: tie -> max (RZ, no OF)"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RP,  pe, pem, inf, 0x05, "e8m0: tie -> +inf (RP, OF)"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RM,  pe, pem, maxf, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "e8m0: tie (pos) -> max (RM, no OF)"),
             # Non-overflow tie: 2^(EMAX-1) + 2^(EMAX-2) -> larger = 2^EMAX (RNE/RP)
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, pem, pe2, pe, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT,
              "e8m0: tie -> larger 2^EMAX (RNE, no OF)"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RZ,  pem, pe2, pem, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "e8m0: tie -> smaller (RZ)"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RP,  pem, pe2, pe, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "e8m0: tie -> larger (RP)"),
             # Cancellation
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, pe, neg(pe), z, 0, "e8m0: 2^EMAX + -2^EMAX = +0"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RM,  pe, neg(pe), zs, 0, "e8m0: cancellation -> -0 (RM)"),
             (OP_SUB, MODE_RNE, pe, neg(pe), inf, 0x05, "e8m0: 2^EMAX - -2^EMAX = inf (OF)"),
             # Opposite-sign d=1: exact 2^EMAX - 2^(EMAX-1) = 2^(EMAX-1)
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, pe, neg(pem), pem, 0, "e8m0: d=1 opposite -> exact 2^(EMAX-1)"),
             # Opposite-sign d=2: tie between 2^(EMAX-1) and 2^EMAX -> larger (RNE/RP)
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, pe, neg(pe2), pe, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT,
              "e8m0: d=2 tie -> larger 2^EMAX (RNE)"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RZ,  pe, neg(pe2), pem, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "e8m0: d=2 tie -> smaller (RZ)"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RP,  pe, neg(pe2), pe, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "e8m0: d=2 tie -> larger (RP)"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RM,  pe, neg(pe2), pem, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "e8m0: d=2 tie -> smaller (RM)"),
             # Opposite-sign d=3: nearest to 2^EMAX (above midpoint)
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, pe, neg(pe3), pe, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT,
              "e8m0: d=3 -> nearest 2^EMAX (RNE, inexact)"),
         ]
     # --- half-way ties (RNE/RNA), binary32 only
     if w == 32:
         p24 = 0x33800000   # 2^-24
         p23 = 0x34000000   # 2^-23
         v += [
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, m1, p23, 0x3F800001, 0, "1 + 2^-23 exact"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, m1, p24, 0x3F800000, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "tie -> even (down)"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNA, m1, p24, 0x3F800001, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "tie -> away"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RZ, m1, p24, 0x3F800000, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "tie -> toward zero"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RP, m1, p24, 0x3F800001, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "tie -> +inf dir"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RM, m1, p24, 0x3F800000, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "tie -> -inf dir"),
             # 1 + 3*2^-24: tie between odd (1+2^-23) and even (1+2^-22) -> even up
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, m1, 0x34400000, 0x3F800002, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "tie -> even (up)"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNA, m1, 0x34400000, 0x3F800002, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "tie -> away"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RZ, m1, 0x34400000, 0x3F800001, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "3/2 ulp -> toward zero"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RM, m1, 0x34400000, 0x3F800001, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "3/2 ulp -> down"),
             # sticky rounding: 1 + 2^-126 + 2^-149 (0x33000001)
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, m1, 0x33000001, 0x3F800000, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT,
              "sticky forces inexact"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RP, m1, 0x33000001, 0x3F800001, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT,
              "sticky rounds up (RP)"),
             # max finite + 2^-24: sticky below max, rounds up over the edge under RP
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RNE, maxf, p24, maxf, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "max + tiny -> max"),
             (OP_ADD, MODE_RP, maxf, p24, inf, 0x05, "max + tiny -> inf under RP"),
         ]
     return v
 
 
 def _directed_mul_vectors(fmt):
     """Hand-verified directed vectors for multiplication (5.4.1)."""
     w = fmt.width
     neg = lambda x: x ^ (1 << (w - 1))
     m0 = fmt.W_MANT
     m1 = _norm1(fmt)          # 1.0
     m1s = neg(m1)
     m2 = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias + 1, 0, fmt)         # 2.0
     m4 = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias + 2, 0, fmt)         # 4.0
     m05 = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias - 1, 0, fmt)        # 0.5
     m025 = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias - 2, 0, fmt)       # 0.25
     maxf = max_finite_bits(0, fmt)
     maxs = neg(maxf)
     maxm = (1 << m0) - 1
     z = encode_zero(0, fmt)
     zs = encode_zero(1, fmt)
     inf = encode_inf(0, fmt)
     infs = encode_inf(1, fmt)
     qnan = encode_nan(0, fmt)
     minn = encode_finite(0, 1, 0, fmt)                  # min normal
     maxsn = encode_finite(0, 0, maxm, fmt)              # max subnormal
     v = []
 
     # --- zero products: sign is the XOR of the operand signs (6.3), and the
     # roundTowardNegative zero-sign quirk of addition does not apply.
     v += [
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, z, z, z, 0, "0 x 0 = +0"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, zs, zs, z, 0, "-0 x -0 = +0"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, zs, z, zs, 0, "-0 x +0 = -0"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, z, zs, zs, 0, "+0 x -0 = -0"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RM, z, zs, zs, 0, "0 x -0 = -0 even under RM (sign XOR)"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, z, m1, z, 0, "0 x 1 = +0"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, zs, m1, zs, 0, "-0 x 1 = -0"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, m2, z, z, 0, "2 x 0 = +0"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, m2, zs, zs, 0, "2 x -0 = -0"),
     ]
 
     # --- infinities (6.3, 7.2e)
     v += [
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, inf, inf, inf, 0, "inf x inf = +inf"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, infs, infs, inf, 0, "-inf x -inf = +inf"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, inf, infs, infs, 0, "inf x -inf = -inf"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, inf, m2, inf, 0, "inf x 2 = +inf"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, m2, infs, infs, 0, "2 x -inf = -inf"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, infs, m05, infs, 0, "-inf x 0.5 = -inf"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, inf, z, qnan, 1 << formats.FLAG_INVALID, "inf x 0 -> qNaN, invalid (7.2e)"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, z, infs, qnan, 1 << formats.FLAG_INVALID, "0 x -inf -> qNaN, invalid (7.2e)"),
     ]
 
     # --- NaNs (6.2.3, 7.2a)
     v += [
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, qnan, m1, qnan, 0, "qNaN x 1 -> qNaN"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, m1, qnan, qnan, 0, "1 x qNaN -> qNaN"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, inf, qnan, qnan, 0, "inf x qNaN -> qNaN"),
     ]
     if w == 32:
         v += [
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, 0x7FC00001, m2, 0x7FC00001, 0, "qNaN payload passthrough"),
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, 0x7F800001, m2, 0x7FC00001, 1 << formats.FLAG_INVALID,
              "sNaN -> qNaN, invalid"),
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, m2, 0xFF80000F, 0x7FC0000F, 1 << formats.FLAG_INVALID,
              "sNaN payload kept, invalid"),
         ]
 
     # --- exact products (RNE)
     v += [
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, m1, m1, m1, 0, "1 x 1 = 1"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, m1, m2, m2, 0, "1 x 2 = 2"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, m2, m2, m4, 0, "2 x 2 = 4"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, m05, m05, m025, 0, "0.5 x 0.5 = 0.25"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, m2, m05, m1, 0, "2 x 0.5 = 1"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, m1s, m1s, m1, 0, "-1 x -1 = 1"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, m1s, m1, m1s, 0, "-1 x 1 = -1"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, m1, m1s, m1s, 0, "1 x -1 = -1"),
     ]
     if fmt.W_MANT > 0:
         # max sub x 2 = 2^emin - 2^(emin-W_MANT+1): an exact normal number
         # (significand 1.11..10 = 2 - 2^(1-W_MANT)).
         v += [
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, maxsn, m2, encode_finite(0, 1, maxm - 1, fmt), 0,
              "max sub x 2 exact"),
         ]
     if fmt.W_MANT >= 3:
         m15 = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias, 1 << (m0 - 1), fmt)      # 1.5
         m3  = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias + 1, 1 << (m0 - 1), fmt)  # 3.0
         m225 = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias + 1, 1 << (m0 - 3), fmt) # 2.25
         u   = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias, 1, fmt)                  # 1 + 2^-W_MANT
         u2  = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias, 2, fmt)                  # 1 + 2^-(W_MANT-1)
         v += [
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, m15, m2, m3, 0, "1.5 x 2 = 3"),
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, m15, m15, m225, 0, "1.5 x 1.5 = 2.25"),
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, m15, m1s, neg(m15), 0, "1.5 x -1 = -1.5"),
             # (1+2^-m)^2 = 1 + 2^-(m-1) + 2^-2m: the 2^-2m tail is sticky only.
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, u, u, u2, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT,
              "(1+2^-m)^2 -> 1+2^-(m-1), inexact"),
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RZ, u, u, u2, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT,
              "(1+2^-m)^2 (RZ) -> 1+2^-(m-1)"),
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RM, u, u, u2, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT,
              "(1+2^-m)^2 (RM, positive) -> 1+2^-(m-1)"),
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RP, u, u, encode_finite(0, fmt.bias, 3, fmt), 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT,
              "(1+2^-m)^2 (RP, positive) -> 1+2^-(m-2), inexact"),
         ]
 
     # --- half-way product tie: (1 + 2^-(m-1)) x (1 + 2^-2) leaves exactly
     # half an ulp. The even-mantissa candidate (RNE/RZ/RM for a positive
     # result) is 2^(m-2) + 2, the odd one (RNA/RP) is 2^(m-2) + 3.
     if fmt.W_MANT >= 3:
         t_a = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias, 2, fmt)                 # 1 + 2^-(m-1)
         t_b = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias, 1 << (m0 - 2), fmt)     # 1 + 2^-2
         t_even = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias, (1 << (m0 - 2)) + 2, fmt)
         t_odd = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias, (1 << (m0 - 2)) + 3, fmt)
         v += [
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, t_a, t_b, t_even, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "tie -> even (down)"),
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RNA, t_a, t_b, t_odd, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "tie -> away (up)"),
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RZ, t_a, t_b, t_even, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "tie -> toward zero"),
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RP, t_a, t_b, t_odd, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "tie -> +inf direction"),
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RM, t_a, t_b, t_even, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT, "tie (pos) -> -inf direction"),
         ]
 
     # --- subnormal / underflow products (7.5, tininess after rounding).
     # Subnormals do not exist for W_MANT = 0 (E8M0).
     if fmt.W_MANT > 0:
         minsn = encode_finite(0, 0, 1, fmt)                        # min subnormal
         psub  = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias - fmt.W_MANT - 1, 0, fmt)  # 2^(-W_MANT-1)
         v += [
             # min normal x 2^(-W_MANT-1) = 2^(emin-W_MANT-1) = half the min
             # subnormal: RNE ties to even (zero); RNA/RP round up to it.
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, minn, psub, z, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT,
              "half min sub (RNE tie -> 0, inexact)"),
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RNA, minn, psub, minsn,
              (1 << formats.FLAG_UNDERFLOW) | (1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT),
              "half min sub (RNA -> min sub, underflow)"),
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RZ, minn, psub, z, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT,
              "half min sub (RZ -> 0, inexact)"),
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RP, minn, psub, minsn,
              (1 << formats.FLAG_UNDERFLOW) | (1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT),
              "half min sub (RP -> min sub, underflow)"),
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RM, minn, psub, z, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT,
              "half min sub (RM, positive -> 0, inexact)"),
             # min normal x min normal = 2^(2emin), far below the min subnormal.
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, minn, minn, z, 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT,
              "min normal x min normal -> 0 (RNE, inexact)"),
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RP, minn, minn, minsn,
              (1 << formats.FLAG_UNDERFLOW) | (1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT),
              "min normal x min normal -> min sub (RP, underflow)"),
         ]
 
     # --- overflow (7.4)
     v += [
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, maxf, maxf, inf, 0x05, "max x max -> +inf (RNE)"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RZ, maxf, maxf, maxf, 0x05, "max x max -> max (RZ)"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RM, maxf, maxf, maxf, 0x05, "max x max -> max (RM, positive)"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RP, maxf, maxf, inf, 0x05, "max x max -> +inf (RP)"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, maxs, maxs, inf, 0x05, "-max x -max -> +inf (RNE)"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, maxs, maxf, infs, 0x05, "-max x max -> -inf (RNE)"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RP, maxs, maxf, maxs, 0x05, "-max x max (RP, negative) -> -max"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RM, maxs, maxf, infs, 0x05, "-max x max (RM, negative) -> -inf"),
         (OP_MUL, MODE_RZ, maxs, maxf, maxs, 0x05, "-max x max (RZ) -> -max"),
     ]
 
     # --- E8M0 (W_MANT = 0): products of exact powers of two (6.3, 7.4).
     if fmt.W_MANT == 0:
         pe  = maxf                                                # 2^EMAX
         p20 = encode_finite(0, 20 + fmt.bias, 0, fmt)             # 2^20
         p40 = encode_finite(0, 40 + fmt.bias, 0, fmt)             # 2^40
         pn100 = encode_finite(0, -100 + fmt.bias, 0, fmt)         # 2^-100
         # Tie at 2^(emin-1): e_a + e_b = emin - 1. For emax = 2^(W_EXP-1)-1
         # (odd), e_a = -(emax-1)/2 and e_b = e_a - 1 give exactly that sum.
         ea = -(fmt.emax - 1) // 2
         eb = ea - 1
         tie_a = encode_finite(0, ea + fmt.bias, 0, fmt)
         tie_b = encode_finite(0, eb + fmt.bias, 0, fmt)
         v += [
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RNE, pe, pe, inf, 0x05, "e8m0: 2^EMAX x 2^EMAX -> inf (RNE, OF)"),
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RZ,  pe, pe, maxf, 0x05, "e8m0: 2^EMAX x 2^EMAX -> max (RZ, OF+INE)"),
             (OP_MUL, MODE_RP,  pe, pe, inf, 0x05, "e8m0: 2^EMAX x 2^EMAX -> inf (RP, OF)"),

 def _directed_div_vectors(fmt):
     """Hand-verified directed vectors for division (5.4.1)."""
     w = fmt.width
     neg = lambda x: x ^ (1 << (w - 1))
     m0 = fmt.W_MANT
     m1 = _norm1(fmt)          # 1.0
     m1s = neg(m1)
     m2 = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias + 1, 0, fmt)         # 2.0
     m4 = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias + 2, 0, fmt)         # 4.0
     m05 = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias - 1, 0, fmt)        # 0.5
     m025 = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias - 2, 0, fmt)       # 0.25
     maxf = max_finite_bits(0, fmt)
     maxs = neg(maxf)
     maxm = (1 << m0) - 1
     z = encode_zero(0, fmt)
     zs = encode_zero(1, fmt)
     inf = encode_inf(0, fmt)
     infs = encode_inf(1, fmt)
     qnan = encode_nan(0, fmt)
     minn = encode_finite(0, 1, 0, fmt)                  # min normal
     maxsn = encode_finite(0, 0, maxm, fmt)              # max subnormal
     minsn = encode_finite(0, 0, 1, fmt)                 # min subnormal
     inv = 1 << formats.FLAG_INVALID
     d0 = 1 << formats.FLAG_DIV0
     ine = 1 << formats.FLAG_INEXACT
     uf = 1 << formats.FLAG_UNDERFLOW
     v = []
 
     # --- zero products/quotients: sign is the XOR of the operand signs (6.3)
     v += [
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, z, m1, z, 0, "0/1 = +0"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, zs, m1, zs, 0, "-0/1 = -0"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, z, m1s, zs, 0, "0/-1 = -0"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1, z, inf, d0, "1/0 -> +inf, div0 (7.3)"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1, zs, infs, d0, "1/-0 -> -inf, div0"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1s, z, infs, d0, "-1/0 -> -inf, div0"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1s, zs, inf, d0, "-1/-0 -> +inf, div0"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, z, z, qnan, inv, "0/0 -> qNaN, invalid (7.2f)"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, z, zs, qnan, inv, "0/-0 -> qNaN, invalid (7.2f)"),
     ]
 
     # --- infinities (6.3, 7.2f)
     v += [
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, inf, m2, inf, 0, "inf/2 = +inf"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, infs, m2, infs, 0, "-inf/2 = -inf"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m2, inf, z, 0, "2/inf = +0"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m2, infs, zs, 0, "2/-inf = -0"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, inf, z, inf, 0, "inf/0 = +inf (not div0)"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, z, inf, z, 0, "0/inf = +0"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, inf, inf, qnan, inv, "inf/inf -> qNaN, invalid (7.2f)"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, infs, infs, qnan, inv, "-inf/-inf -> qNaN, invalid"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, inf, infs, qnan, inv, "inf/-inf -> qNaN, invalid"),
     ]
 
     # --- NaNs (6.2.3, 7.2a). Only meaningful where NaN encodings exist.
     if fmt.W_MANT > 0:
         v += [
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, qnan, m1, qnan, 0, "qNaN/1 -> qNaN"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1, qnan, qnan, 0, "1/qNaN -> qNaN"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, inf, qnan, qnan, 0, "inf/qNaN -> qNaN"),
         ]
     if w == 32:
         v += [
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, 0x7FC00001, m2, 0x7FC00001, 0, "qNaN payload passthrough"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, 0x7F800001, m2, 0x7FC00001, inv, "sNaN -> qNaN, invalid"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m2, 0xFF80000F, 0x7FC0000F, inv, "sNaN payload kept, invalid"),
         ]
 
     # --- exact quotients (RNE)
     v += [
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1, m1, m1, 0, "1/1 = 1"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m2, m1, m2, 0, "2/1 = 2"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1, m2, m05, 0, "1/2 = 0.5"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m4, m2, m2, 0, "4/2 = 2"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m05, m2, m025, 0, "0.5/2 = 0.25"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1, m05, m2, 0, "1/0.5 = 2"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1s, m1s, m1, 0, "-1/-1 = 1"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1s, m1, m1s, 0, "-1/1 = -1"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1, m1s, m1s, 0, "1/-1 = -1"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, maxf, m1, maxf, 0, "max/1 = max"),
     ]
     if fmt.W_MANT >= 3:
         m15 = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias, 1 << (m0 - 1), fmt)      # 1.5
         m3  = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias + 1, 1 << (m0 - 1), fmt)  # 3.0
         inv1 = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias, 1, fmt)                 # 1 + 2^-W_MANT
         below1 = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias - 1, (1 << m0) - 2, fmt)  # 1 - 2^-W_MANT
         up1 = encode_finite(0, fmt.bias - 1, (1 << m0) - 1, fmt)  # 1 - 2^-(W_MANT+1)
         v += [
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m15, m3, m05, 0, "1.5/3 = 0.5"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m3, m15, m2, 0, "3/1.5 = 2"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m15, m1s, neg(m15), 0, "1.5/-1 = -1.5"),
             # 1/(1+2^-m) = 1 - 2^-m + 2^-2m - ...: on the [0.5,1) grid the
             # value is 2^m - 2 + 2^-m ulps, so RNE/RZ/RM drop to 1 - 2^-m and
             # RP rounds up to 1 - 2^-(m+1).
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1, inv1, below1, ine, "1/(1+2^-m) -> 1-2^-m (RNE, inexact)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RZ,  m1, inv1, below1, ine, "1/(1+2^-m) -> 1-2^-m (RZ)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RM,  m1, inv1, below1, ine, "1/(1+2^-m) (pos) -> 1-2^-m (RM)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RP,  m1, inv1, up1, ine, "1/(1+2^-m) (RP) -> 1-2^-(m+1), inexact"),
         ]
 
     # --- inexact / tie rounding, binary32 only
     if w == 32:
         v += [
             # 1/3 = 0.3333... -> mantissa 0x2AAAAAB (round up) / 0x2AAAAAA (down).
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m1, 0x40400000, 0x3EAAAAAB, ine, "1/3 -> up (RNE)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNA, m1, 0x40400000, 0x3EAAAAAB, ine, "1/3 -> up (RNA)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RZ,  m1, 0x40400000, 0x3EAAAAAA, ine, "1/3 -> down (RZ)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RP,  m1, 0x40400000, 0x3EAAAAAB, ine, "1/3 -> up (RP)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RM,  m1, 0x40400000, 0x3EAAAAAA, ine, "1/3 (pos) -> down (RM)"),
             # 2/3 = 0.666... = 1.333...*2^-1 -> mantissa 0x2AAAAB, exp 0x7E.
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, m2, 0x40400000, 0x3F2AAAAB, ine, "2/3 -> up (RNE)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RZ,  m2, 0x40400000, 0x3F2AAAAA, ine, "2/3 -> down (RZ)"),
         ]
 
     # --- subnormal / underflow quotients (7.5, tininess after rounding).
     # Subnormals do not exist for W_MANT = 0 (E8M0).
     if fmt.W_MANT > 0:
         # min normal / 2 = 2^(emin-1): an exact subnormal (significand 2^(W_MANT-1)).
         v += [
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, minn, m2, encode_finite(0, 0, 1 << (m0 - 1), fmt), 0,
              "min normal/2 = exact subnormal"),
         ]
         # min sub / 2 = 2^(emin-W_MANT-1) = half the min subnormal: RNE tie -> 0.
         v += [
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, minsn, m2, z, ine, "min sub/2 (RNE tie -> 0, inexact)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNA, minsn, m2, minsn, uf | ine, "min sub/2 (RNA -> min sub, underflow)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RZ,  minsn, m2, z, ine, "min sub/2 (RZ -> 0, inexact)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RP,  minsn, m2, minsn, uf | ine, "min sub/2 (RP -> min sub, underflow)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RM,  minsn, m2, z, ine, "min sub/2 (RM, positive -> 0, inexact)"),
             # max sub / 2 = (2^W_MANT-1)/2 ulps: RNE tie -> even (up), RZ down.
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, maxsn, m2, encode_finite(0, 0, 1 << (m0 - 1), fmt), uf | ine,
              "max sub/2 (RNE tie -> even up, underflow)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RZ,  maxsn, m2, encode_finite(0, 0, (1 << (m0 - 1)) - 1, fmt), uf | ine,
              "max sub/2 (RZ -> down, underflow)"),
         ]
 
     # --- overflow (7.4): dividing by a value < 1 inflates the quotient.
     v += [
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, maxf, m05, inf, 0x05, "max/0.5 -> +inf (RNE)"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RZ,  maxf, m05, maxf, 0x05, "max/0.5 -> max (RZ)"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RM,  maxf, m05, maxf, 0x05, "max/0.5 -> max (RM, positive)"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RP,  maxf, m05, inf, 0x05, "max/0.5 -> +inf (RP)"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, maxs, m05, infs, 0x05, "-max/0.5 -> -inf (RNE)"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RP,  maxs, m05, maxs, 0x05, "-max/0.5 (RP, negative) -> -max"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RM,  maxs, m05, infs, 0x05, "-max/0.5 (RM, negative) -> -inf"),
         (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, maxf, m025, inf, 0x05, "max/0.25 -> +inf (RNE)"),
     ]
 
     # --- E8M0 (W_MANT = 0): quotients of exact powers of two (6.3, 7.3, 7.4).
     if fmt.W_MANT == 0:
         pe  = maxf                                                # 2^EMAX
         p10 = encode_finite(0, 10 + fmt.bias, 0, fmt)             # 2^10
         p5  = encode_finite(0, 5 + fmt.bias, 0, fmt)              # 2^5
         p15 = encode_finite(0, 15 + fmt.bias, 0, fmt)             # 2^15
         pn5 = encode_finite(0, -5 + fmt.bias, 0, fmt)             # 2^-5
         pn100 = encode_finite(0, -100 + fmt.bias, 0, fmt)         # 2^-100
         # Tie at 2^(emin-1): e_a - e_b = emin - 1. For emax = 2^(W_EXP-1)-1
         # (odd), e_a = -(emax-1)/2 and e_b = e_a + emax give exactly that.
         ea = -(fmt.emax - 1) // 2
         eb = ea + fmt.emax
         tie_a = encode_finite(0, ea + fmt.bias, 0, fmt)
         tie_b = encode_finite(0, eb + fmt.bias, 0, fmt)
         v += [
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, p10, p5, p5, 0, "e8m0: 2^10/2^5 = 2^5"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, p10, pn5, p15, 0, "e8m0: 2^10/2^-5 = 2^15"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, pe, pn100, inf, 0x05, "e8m0: 2^EMAX/2^-100 -> inf (RNE, OF)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RZ,  pe, pn100, maxf, 0x05, "e8m0: 2^EMAX/2^-100 -> max (RZ, OF+INE)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, pn100, pe, z, ine, "e8m0: tiny quotient -> 0 (RNE, inexact)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RP,  pn100, pe, minn, ine, "e8m0: tiny quotient -> 2^emin (RP, inexact)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, tie_a, tie_b, z, ine, "e8m0: half-2^emin tie -> 0 (RNE, inexact)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNA, tie_a, tie_b, minn, ine, "e8m0: half-2^emin tie -> 2^emin (RNA)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RP,  tie_a, tie_b, minn, ine, "e8m0: half-2^emin tie -> 2^emin (RP)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RM,  tie_a, tie_b, z, ine, "e8m0: half-2^emin tie (pos) -> 0 (RM)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, pe, pe, m1, 0, "e8m0: 2^EMAX/2^EMAX = 1"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, inf, z, inf, 0, "e8m0: inf/0 -> +inf (not div0)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, z, z, inf, inv, "e8m0: 0/0 -> +inf, invalid (7.2f)"),
             (OP_DIV, MODE_RNE, pe, z, inf, d0, "e8m0: 2^EMAX/0 -> +inf, div0 (7.3)"),
         ]
     return v
